title: California's 17th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 17th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Ro Khanna against Republican challenger Ritesh Tandon. Khanna, first elected in 2016, is seeking a sixth term representing a district that covers much of Silicon Valley, including parts of Santa Clara and Alameda counties. The race was shaped by the June 2 top-two primary, in which Khanna won 62.3% of the vote and Tandon finished second with 14.8%, advancing both to the general election. Cook Political Report has rated the general election as Solidly Democratic, reflecting the district's strong Democratic lean, though Tandon is campaigning on affordability and innovation-focused policies.
polling_note: No general election polls were found for CA-17 as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report rated the race as Solidly Democratic before the primary.

candidates.name: Ro Khanna
candidates.summary: Ro Khanna is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 17th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. A leading progressive voice in the House, he serves as Vice Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and focuses on American manufacturing, technology leadership, and working-class economic issues. He authored the Endless Frontier Act, which formed the basis for the CHIPS and Science Act, and has refused contributions from PACs and lobbyists.

candidates.name: Ritesh Tandon
candidates.summary: Ritesh Tandon is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in California's 17th Congressional District. An engineer and entrepreneur with an MBA and Master of Computer Engineering from Santa Clara University, he has spent 26 years in the Bay Area and works as a Research Fellow at the Haas School of Business, UC Berkeley. He advanced from the June 2 primary with 14.8% of the vote and campaigns on affordability, innovation, border security, and an America First economic agenda.
